design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (homeowner_claims_and_replacement), revision 5

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems 1, factor_counts [6, 4]. The stalled-repair replacement (homeplan_ext_stalled_repair_replacement) takes 6 factors, the customer's cash (homeplan_ext_customer_elected_cash) takes 4. Task 1's draw: prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [6, 5, 4].

[Revision 5 log] The homeplan render and the round-4 audit raised source-quotation and coverage points on the charter, none of which moves this task's figures: every replaced_by of the stalled-repair and customer-elected policies now restates the parts of its retired base clause that stay in force — the shared item cap, the aggregate counting of every payment, the remaining item and aggregate benefits, the cash's benefit limits and rounding, its settlement_basis, and the fees that are still not refunded.

[Revision 4 log] Policy audit round 3 passed this task and recorded two observations on its stalled-repair rule: O-r3-1 (a water heater's connection charge contradicted 'replacement cost = equipment plus installation') and O-r3-2 (a missed contact on the household's own homeowner-contract requests should count toward the repeat tier first). Changes, none of which moves this task's figures: (a) the water-line connection charge now pays only hook-ups outside standard installation — a refrigerator's ice-maker and dispenser line, a dishwasher's or clothes washer's new supply and drain hoses — and nothing for a water heater, whose connections are part of the contracted installation; (b) the repeat tier of the missed-contact credit now counts an earlier missed-contact re-dispatch on another of the household's homeowner-contract requests first and then one on a rider request; this household has none of the former in the twelve months, so the rider's February re-dispatch still decides the tier.

[Revision 3 log] Policy audit round 2 found: R2-F1 (the interior-line hookup ladder had an unreachable middle tier, since every line plan that covers interior supply lines carries a 3000.00 limit, and its tiers were one coordination formula; connecting a new unit is installation, not a line failure), R2-F3 (with that ladder struck no cross-difficulty factor remained), O-r2-2 (the base remaining-benefit sentence was not named in the overwrites) and O-r2-4 (the cash carries a disposal addition although the base allowance rule says allowances are never paid on a cash-in-lieu settlement). Changes: (a) the line-plan ladder is gone; the replacement now carries a water-line connection charge decided by the item (a water heater's supply and relief connections, a single supply line for a refrigerator, dishwasher or clothes washer, nothing otherwise; revision 4 narrowed it to hook-ups outside standard installation); (b) the missed-contact credit is now the cross-difficulty factor: its repeat tier applies when a request under a Bridgewell coverage rider the customer holds was also re-dispatched after a missed contact window within the twelve months before today, so the stalled request's miss is the same appliance network failing the same household again; the world gained the customer's Second Refrigerator Rider (garage refrigerator) and its February request, which Hoosier Appliance Doctors missed and Northside Appliance Repair then took over; (c) every policy names the base remaining-benefit sentence in its scoped overwrite; (d) the cash policy declares a scoped overwrite of the base sentence 'Allowances are never paid on a cash-in-lieu settlement or an out-of-network reimbursement, because Bridgewell performs no installation there.' for its disposal addition, and books no allowance row; (e) the line plan was removed from this world, since no rule of this task reads it any more. Round-2 changes kept: the twelve-month window with its declared overwrites, the re-priced like-unit cost as the recorded replacement_cost, the prerequisite sentence naming both states, the re-drawn tool suffix and the docstrings without ordering words.

[Why this is a good test] A homeowner asks only for cash toward a new refrigerator. The cash rule says a customer-elected settlement is fixed only after a replacement authorization that carries neither a reversal nor a completion report stands on the request; the records show only a reversed repair authorization (stalled 38 days, then declined). The agent must read the stalled-repair rule, see that the reversed stalled repair obliges Bridgewell to authorize a replacement (parts_unavailable), compute that payment from six rules (one of them read from the customer's rider records) against the refrigerator cap, record it, and then compute the customer-elected cash from the new authorization with four more rules and hand the election to the customer.

[Scope snapshot] Claimed here: homeplan_ext_stalled_repair_replacement (tool authorize_stalled_repair_replacement_b6f80e12, agent) and homeplan_ext_customer_elected_cash (tool elect_cash_in_place_of_replacement_7cf483ad, user). Task 1 claims the haul-away allowance, the company-elected offer and its acceptance; nothing is shared.

[Problem-tree card] root homeplan_ext_customer_elected_cash <- homeplan_ext_stalled_repair_replacement; kind value_input; gate binding live_replacement_amount; form state; prerequisite sentence (in the cash policy's own rule): "A customer-elected cash settlement on a service request is fixed only after a replacement authorization that carries neither a reversal nor a completion report stands on that request." Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; waits on a record-visible state (a replacement authorization with neither a reversal nor a completion report on the request); names no tool, id or code token; strength "is fixed only after" matches the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty creates replacement authorizations: the stalled-repair replacement tool. Unmet at frozen_time: the request carries only repair authorization 1260828265, reversed on 2026-10-05, and no replacement authorization exists on the contract. Resolving owner: agent; the root is the customer's own write (owner=user). Topological order: replacement (step 11), cash (step 13). Deletion sensitivity: skipping step 11 -> the cash computation cannot be evaluated at all, because with no replacement authorization on the contract there is no amount and no item to start from; with it the cash is 2562.1.

[Base-invariant card] Replacement write: homeplan_evt_repair_or_replace.covered_determination_on_file — a covered determination on the same request; one_open_authorization_per_request — the repair authorization is reversed; homeplan_evt_benefit_caps has no gate (policy_scope). Declared overwrites: the amount sentence of homeplan_evt_repair_or_replace (scoped to a replacement after a stalled repair) and the four benefit_caps sentences (term anchor, shared item cap, aggregate counting, remaining benefits), scoped to the same replacement. Cash write: homeplan_evt_cash_in_lieu.one_cash_settlement_per_request — no cash payment exists on the request; the offer-validity time gate is retired for customer-elected settlements by a scoped overwrite (no offer is issued for them), so no time gate is in play (temporal_feasibility []); the allowance-on-cash sentence of homeplan_evt_supplemental_allowances is overwritten for the cash's disposal addition, scoped to customer-elected settlements.

[Business-object card] Target: the August 24 refrigerator request 3b60f6a9-14f8-4901-8de6-c9f4643c3d6f on contract 9d2ffc67-6161-4db3-bd21-4f09922fbfe4. Refrigerator payments dated after 2025-10-14: 340.00 (January repair), 455.00 (May repair), 880.00 (August repair) and its reversal -880.00 -> 795.00; the aggregate adds the garbage disposal reimbursements 265.00 (2025-10-20) and 190.00 (2026-03-12) -> 1250.00. The rider's 185.00 repair is a rider benefit and counts toward no homeplan cap. Correlation keys: homeplan_service_request_id and the reversed authorization number 1260828265.

[Factor card — replacement, 6 factors] (1) price_list_escalation, parameter: cost recorded 47 days ago -> 0.02 (baseline -> 2535.0). (2) water_line_connection_ladder, parameter: a refrigerator's ice-maker and dispenser line is an add-on hook-up -> 65.00 (baseline none -> 2509.6). (3) stall_day_count_basis, method: routine request, Platinum contact window 24h -> days after authorization through reversal = 38 -> 190.00 (baseline none -> 2384.6); near-miss: counting from the request date would give 42, a count reserved for emergency requests. (4) missed_contact_ladder, parameter, multi-source and cross-difficulty (addon): a missed-contact re-dispatch on the stalled request, none on the household's other homeowner-contract requests in the window, and one on the Second Refrigerator Rider request of 2026-02-09 -> repeat credit 150.00 (baseline none -> 2424.6); near-miss: reading only the homeplan records gives the single-miss 75.00. (5) attached_dwelling_carry_in, parameter, multi-source (contract dwelling type x the request's item): townhome and refrigerator -> 60.00 (baseline -> 2514.6). (6) install_window_premium, parameter: after-hours window on a tier with no customer surcharge -> 90.00 (baseline -> 2484.6). Whole baseline: 1980.0. Gold 2574.6.

[Factor card — cash, 4 factors] (1) cash_starting_figure_basis, method: refrigerator -> recorded amount less 300.00 delivery and connection (baseline: recorded amount -> 2705.0, where the remaining refrigerator benefit binds). (2) stall_fee_share_ladder, parameter: 38-day stall -> half of the 125.00 visit fee (baseline -> 2499.6). (3) regulated_disposal_ladder, parameter: the old refrigerator needs certified refrigerant recovery -> 75.00 (baseline -> 2487.1). (4) food_spoilage_ladder, parameter: refrigerator out of service 51 days -> 150.00 (baseline -> 2412.1). Whole baseline: 2574.6. Gold 2562.1.

[Rows and why they exist] Customer; Platinum townhome contract (tier, dwelling type, address); the Second Refrigerator Rider on the contract with its February request, two assignments (Hoosier Appliance Doctors missed the contact window, Northside Appliance Repair was re-dispatched), covered determination and repair authorization (the cross-difficulty repeat-miss evidence); two network appliance contractors (the missed contact of Hoosier Appliance Doctors on the August request and the re-dispatch to Northside Appliance Repair, and the evidence that the settlement is customer-elected); five requests (three refrigerator, two garbage disposal); claim events (dispatches, determinations, the two completed refrigerator repairs, the stalled repair and its reversal, the garbage disposal reimbursements); billing (three 2026 installments with their payments and five visit fees — the August one is the stall-fee base). No automatic clause fires: premium is paid, the renewal notice is issued, no allowance or offer is owed.

[Persona design] Philippa volunteers the surface goal (cash toward a new refrigerator), the history the records hold (approved repair, back-ordered part, cancelled on October 5th) and her hard preference (no further repair, no installation). Identity, dates and the fact that the refrigerator stayed out of use come only when asked. She never mentions the garage refrigerator or its February visit. Passive branches: she lets the agent do Bridgewell-side steps, declines installation, runs the handed-over tool with the agent's details, and closes once the cash is confirmed.

[Most likely mistakes] (1) Answering the cash request without the replacement authorization the cash rule waits on. (2) Treating the request as company-elected although two non-suspended appliance contractors serve 46220. (3) Counting stall days from the request date (42) instead of the authorization date (38). (4) Paying the single-miss credit because the rider's claim history was never read. (5) Writing the payment or the bare recorded cost (1980.00) as the authorization's replacement_cost instead of the re-priced like-unit cost the rule names. (6) Forgetting to take the new replacement amount back out of the refrigerator usage when capping the cash.

[Standard solution] Locate (full name) -> verify (phone + ZIP) -> read contract, requests, claim history, billing, appliance contractors, the contract's riders, the rider's requests and its claim history -> unlock/call the stalled-repair replacement tool with request 3b60f6a9-14f8-4901-8de6-c9f4643c3d6f, refrigerator, 880.00, 2019.6, 2574.6 -> unlock the cash election tool and hand it to the customer with authorization RPA-760fdc8a0cd8, 2574.6 and 2562.1.

[Verification run] sim.py (check_compute's build_env/eval_compute on the replayed world): replacement 2574.6, baseline 1980.0, factor baselines [('price_list_escalation', 2535.0), ('water_line_connection_ladder', 2509.6), ('stall_day_count_basis', 2384.6), ('missed_contact_ladder', 2424.6), ('attached_dwelling_carry_in', 2514.6), ('install_window_premium', 2484.6)]; cash after step 11 2562.1, baseline 2574.6, factor baselines [('cash_starting_figure_basis', 2705.0), ('stall_fee_share_ladder', 2499.6), ('regulated_disposal_ladder', 2487.1), ('food_spoilage_ladder', 2412.1)]; skipped prerequisite: cannot be evaluated at all, because with no replacement authorization on the contract there is no amount and no item to start from.

[Closure] homeplan_ext_stalled_repair_replacement -> authorize_stalled_repair_replacement_b6f80e12 -> computations[0] step 11 amount -> new replacement row; homeplan_ext_customer_elected_cash -> elect_cash_in_place_of_replacement_7cf483ad -> computations[1] step 13 cash_amount -> payment and reversal rows. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies = [homeplan_ext_stalled_repair_replacement, homeplan_ext_customer_elected_cash].

[Gate run] check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding, check_cross_fire: OK per task and difficulty-wide; check_traceability: the only misses are the two unlock tool names, which become reachable once the KB is rendered.
user_scenario:
You are Philippa Duquesne-Arkwright, a retired school librarian in Indianapolis who has kept a Bridgewell homeowner plan on her townhome at 5418 Bramblewood Court for about seven years. You speak politely but you are tired of this saga and you say so. Your kitchen refrigerator gave out again in late August. Bridgewell approved a repair, but the technician kept telling you the part was on back order, and after more than five weeks of keeping groceries in a cooler you phoned on October 5th and told them to forget the repair. This refrigerator has already been fixed twice this year and you do not want anyone repairing it again. You open the call by explaining that in your own words and asking whether Bridgewell can simply give you cash toward a new refrigerator that you pick out yourself; you are not interested in waiting for anyone to install one.

When the agent asks for your name you give it as Philippa Duquesne-Arkwright. When asked to confirm who you are, you give the phone number on your account, 3175550107, and your ZIP code, 46220; only if a further detail is needed do you add your email, pduquesne.arkwright@lanternmail.com. You do not know your contract or service request numbers and you tell the agent they are on file under your name and the Bramblewood Court address. If the agent asks when the trouble started you say the refrigerator quit around August 24th, and if asked when you cancelled the repair you say it was October 5th. If asked, you say the refrigerator has been out of use the whole time since then.

You are happy to let the agent take care of whatever Bridgewell has to do on its side, and if the agent says something has to be put on record before the cash can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead. If the agent offers to have a new refrigerator installed instead, you say no, you would rather have the cash. When the agent tells you how much cash you would receive, you listen, and if the agent hands you the step to accept the cash yourself, you carry it out with exactly the details the agent gives you and read back the confirmation you get. If the agent only describes the figure without giving you anything to accept, you ask how you go about accepting it. Once the agent confirms the cash has been recorded for you, you thank them and say goodbye.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's customer profile from the full name she states.

edges.condition: The service request carries a homeplan_replacement_authorization row whose authorization_number is neither named as reversed_authorization_number on a homeplan_authorization_reversal row nor named on a homeplan_work_completion row.
edges.policy_source: A customer-elected cash settlement on a service request is fixed only after a replacement authorization that carries neither a reversal nor a completion report stands on that request.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time the August 24 refrigerator request carries only a repair authorization (1260828265), and that authorization is reversed; no replacement authorization exists anywhere on the contract, so none stands on the request.
evidence: initial_state.homeplan_claim_events.647c0e73-99a4-4fc2-a42c-51907083a128.event_type = homeplan_repair_authorization (the other refrigerator authorizations on the contract are repairs too)
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The stalled-repair replacement authorization written at step 11 adds a homeplan_replacement_authorization row on the request (authorization RPA-760fdc8a0cd8, amount 2574.6) with neither a reversal nor a completion report; live_replacement_amount becomes 2574.6 and the cash computes to 2562.1.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single edge (cash <- replacement), so only one topological order exists: the replacement authorization first, then the customer's cash election. The reverse order cannot be carried out, because the cash names and reverses the replacement authorization the first write creates.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 11 leaves no replacement authorization on the contract: the cash computation cannot be evaluated at all, because with no replacement authorization on the contract there is no amount and no item to start from, and the terminal state lacks the replacement row while the cash settlement could not name a standing authorization; with step 11 the cash is 2562.1.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions a replacement authorization, a replacement being put on record, parts_unavailable or any Bridgewell-side step; the customer only asks for cash toward a new refrigerator and says, passively, that the agent may go ahead if something has to be put on record first.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: elect_cash_in_place_of_replacement_7cf483ad writes the payment and the reversal with whatever authorization number and amounts it receives; it never looks for a standing replacement authorization, never refuses and never warns (its body is two ctx.create calls and a return). authorize_stalled_repair_replacement_b6f80e12 likewise writes one row without checking the request's state.
